proposed.text: Under PD 1096, what are the two specific criteria used to evaluate whether a change of occupancy triggers the 'more hazardous' compliance pathway?

options.text: Construction cost of the proposed renovation and the age of the existing building
Life risk to occupants and fire risk associated with the proposed new use
Proximity to adjacent structures and the occupant load of the proposed new use
Structural rating of the building and the zoning classification of the lot

proposed.rationale: Sec. 702 specifies that the determination of whether a change constitutes a more or less hazardous reclassification is based on two criteria: LIFE RISK (the risk of injury or death to the occupants) and FIRE RISK (the probability and severity of fire in the new use). Both factors must be considered together. Construction cost, building age, and structural rating are not the evaluative criteria under Sec. 702.
proposed.explanation: LIFE RISK + FIRE RISK = the dual criteria. These map directly to the two primary safety concerns that building codes are designed to address: protecting occupants from structural/panic hazards (life risk) and from fire (fire risk).
